text.p: Shareholders of NationsBank Corp voted on Friday to approve a merger with Boatmen's Bancshares Inc of St. Louis, creating the nation's fourth-largest bank with some $230 billion in assets.

Shareholders overwhelmingly approved the merger at a special meeting on Friday, and bank officials said they hoped to complete the merger in January 1997. The chairman of the merged bank will be Andrew Craig of Botatmen's, and the chief executive officer will be Hugh McColl of NationsBank.

The merger had been opposed by some community activist groups that expressed concern the merged banks would leave low-income neighborhoods underserved. But the U.S. Federal Reserve approved the merger earlier this month, saying both companies had a track record of serving poorer neighborhoods.
The merger, valued by analysts at some $9 billion, will let NationsBank extend its operations into the midwest and operate in a total of 16 U.S. states and the District of Columbia.
NationsBank is the fifth-largest bank in the United States with assets of $192.3 billion, while Boatmen's is the 24th largest U.S. bank with assets of $40.7 billion.
